title: A Blood Glucose Control Framework Based on Reinforcement Learning With Safety and Interpretability: In Silico Validation
domain: Type 1 diabetes; automated insulin delivery; in-silico control
dataset_or_cohort: UVA/Padova Type 1 Diabetes Simulator virtual adult and adolescent populations
sample_scale: 20 virtual subjects (10 adults and 10 adolescents), each simulated for 20 days with four or five randomized meals per day
institution_count: NA: simulator study with no clinical institution or patient recruitment
split_strategy: Online predictors use the trailing 250 minutes; prediction and control are evaluated in the same simulator subjects, with no independent subject-level or external split
observation_process: Glucose, delivered insulin, meal intake, and time information sampled every 5 minutes; the controller state includes a 60-minute history window
missingness: NA: simulator observations are generated as complete trajectories; no missing-data mechanism reported
censoring_or_competing_events: NA: no censoring, death, or competing event in the virtual-subject experiment
state: Glucose, insulin, meal, and time features plus a nine-dimensional DAN-derived contextual state
observation_decoder: Random-forest regression directly forecasts glucose; auxiliary deep architecture processes the extended state for policy learning
action: Continuous insulin delivery with safety-actor suspension/additional-insulin commands and oral-carbohydrate rescue
action_provenance: SAC-selected simulated pump commands; PID guides the initial control period and the rule-based safety actor can override unsafe commands
transition_mechanism: Online random-forest and DAN glucose predictors support imagined SAC rollouts; the random forest supplies point forecasts and DAN extends the state context
maximum_horizon: 30-minute glucose prediction, 45-minute safety look-ahead, 150-minute imagined rollout, and 20-day closed-loop evaluation
rollout_regime: Free-running imagined rollout inside the controller and closed-loop operation in the UVA/Padova simulator.
capability_claim: Planning — sequential insulin control optimized through model rollouts with an explicit safety layer.
baselines: PID controller and algorithm/component comparisons reported in the article
state_fidelity_metrics: Thirty-minute glucose MAE plus TIR, TBR, TAR, median glucose, and CVGA control zones
transition_metrics: Thirty-minute MAE: adolescents 28.1±19.1 mg/dL (DAN) and 13.3±13.9 (RFR); adults 21.8±15.4 and 12.4±11.7; no error-versus-horizon curve
rollout_stability: Twenty-day closed-loop trajectories remain controlled, but error or control performance is not resolved across rollout horizons
action_sensitivity: No structured action-removal or dose-perturbation study; PID comparison does not isolate action information in the transition model
calibration_and_uncertainty: Prediction errors and across-subject summaries are reported; no formal reliability, coverage, calibration slope, or calibrated predictive interval
external_validation: No external cohort, clinical device, or independent simulator validation
decision_utility: Closed-loop simulated glucose control versus PID, including time in target ranges and CVGA outcomes.
safety_evaluation: Predicted-glucose rules suspend insulin below 70 mg/dL and add insulin above 180 mg/dL; hypoglycemia outcomes are reported in simulation only
statistical_analysis: Descriptive mean and variability across 10 virtual subjects and prediction-error summaries; no clearly reported inferential hypothesis test
causal_language: The article motivates safe control but does not make an identified causal treatment-effect claim
estimand: NA: no causal estimand; objective is closed-loop glycemic control
confounding_strategy: NA: simulator policy experiment rather than observational causal estimation
positivity_and_overlap: NA: no treatment-overlap estimand; explored insulin support is not formally characterized
counterfactual_validation: No real-patient counterfactual validation; only virtual-subject closed-loop behavior
code_access: NI: no public paper-specific source-code repository identified in the full text
weights_access: NI: trained model weights are not reported as publicly available
data_access: Simulator-generated data are not released; UVA/Padova simulator access is separately governed
preprocessing_reproducibility: The 5-minute sampling, 60-minute history, feature construction, model architecture, reward, and safety rules are described; reusable preprocessing artifacts are NI
randomness: Stochastic RL and virtual meals are used; random seeds and a complete seed protocol are NI
evidence_anchors: Official IEEE Access article, DOI 10.1109/ACCESS.2021.3100007: Methods Sec. III and Algorithms 1-3; Experiments Sec. IV, Tables 1-4, Figs. 3-7; Appendices A-B.
appraisal_strengths: Clear action-conditioned transition model, long closed-loop simulator evaluation, clinically interpretable glucose outcomes, and explicit safety overrides
appraisal_limitations: Simulation-only evidence in the same virtual populations; no independent validation, calibrated uncertainty, or horizon-resolved rollout-fidelity analysis
source_status: Full official IEEE version-of-record PDF inspected

title: A Data-Driven Closed-Loop Control Approach to Drive Neural State Transitions for Mechanistic Insight.
publication_status: Peer-reviewed journal article; Human Brain Mapping; 2026
domain: Neuroimaging; affective neuroscience; individualized fMRI dynamics and control
dataset_or_cohort: Reanalysis of Zamoscik et al. remitted major depressive disorder cohort from Heidelberg
sample_scale: 60 participants: 30 remitted MDD and 30 matched healthy controls; two 4.5-minute scans per person
institution_count: 1 institution/source cohort
split_strategy: Within each participant and condition, the first 120 time points trained the DSR model and the final 40 formed the test segment; five independently initialized models were fitted and the lowest-test-loss model was selected, so the test segment participated in model selection.
observation_process: 3 T Siemens fMRI; TR 1.5 seconds; rest and sad-mood induction; 11 bilateral ROIs reduced to 66 principal-component features
missingness: No explicit missing-data model was reported; preprocessing produced complete modeled segments after nuisance removal and band-pass filtering.
censoring_or_competing_events: NA: no clinical time-to-event outcome; each scan is a fixed-length sequence
state: Individual nonlinear latent neural state reconstructed by a shallow piecewise-linear recurrent neural network from 66 regional principal-component signals.
observation_decoder: A linear decoder maps latent state to 66-dimensional regional fMRI observations; affective target states are represented by Gaussian-mixture distributions.
action: Additive state-dependent latent control restricted globally or to selected regions
action_provenance: Simulated model control; not an administered physiological stimulation
transition_mechanism: Individual shallow piecewise-linear recurrent neural dynamics coupled to an optimized state-feedback controller toward a Gaussian-mixture target.
maximum_horizon: Main controlled trajectories run T=D+11 steps with D=10 (21 steps total, approximately 31.5 s at TR 1.5 s); D=5 is reported as a sensitivity analysis. The DSR train/test segments contain 120/40 observed points per condition.
rollout_regime: Free generative reconstruction and simulated closed-loop control from empirical initial states
capability_claim: Planning: optimize controls that move reconstructed brain dynamics between rest and sad-mood targets
baselines: Uncontrolled (zero-control) dynamics, rMDD-versus-healthy-control models, and 11 region-restricted control solutions; no separate action-agnostic learned predictive model.
state_fidelity_metrics: Held-out reconstruction, power-spectrum Hellinger distance, and empirical-versus-reconstructed functional-connectivity agreement.
transition_metrics: Target negative log likelihood over controlled trajectories, cumulative control energy, target convergence, and Lyapunov characterization of reconstructed dynamics.
rollout_stability: Target likelihood is traced over controlled trajectories and conclusions are stress-tested at D=5 versus D=10; no formal long-horizon drift, joint-state coherence, or physiological constraint-violation audit.
action_sensitivity: Zero-control comparison, control restricted to each of 11 bilateral regions, and control-horizon/regularization sensitivity; no empirical stimulation-response validation.
calibration_and_uncertainty: Variation across independently initialized models is examined, but no reliability, ECE, calibration slope, predictive interval, or interval-coverage calibration is reported.
external_validation: No external, temporal, or institutional validation; authors identify single-dataset generalizability as a limitation
decision_utility: Simulated target attainment and energy quantify control feasibility; no clinician or patient decision outcome
safety_evaluation: No clinical hazard, physiological constraint, failure-recovery, or override evaluation
statistical_analysis: Mann-Whitney U tests, Pearson correlations, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control, and IQR outlier handling
causal_language: Authors describe model-based causal intervention analyses and mechanistic insight, but interventions occur only in a learned latent model
estimand: Model-specific individual controlled trajectory and target proximity; no identified real-world treatment-effect estimand
confounding_strategy: NA: the study does not estimate a real stimulation treatment effect; simulated latent controls have no design-based confounding adjustment.
positivity_and_overlap: NI: overlap/support for latent controls was not evaluated
counterfactual_validation: Only internal model interventions and regional perturbations; no randomized or empirical counterfactual validation
code_access: Public code and analysis repository: https://github.com/humml-lab/fmri-control; MIT license
weights_access: Unclear: checkpoint-consuming scripts are present, but study-specific trained weights were not clearly released
data_access: Paper reports fully preprocessed data with the code; raw participant data access is governed by the original study
preprocessing_reproducibility: Detailed ROI, PCA, filtering, model-training, and control procedures plus public analysis code/preprocessed arrays; reconstruction from raw scanner data is only partial.
randomness: Five Xavier-initialized models per participant; best test loss selected; fixed random seeds not reported
evidence_anchors: Human Brain Mapping PMCID PMC13370802: Methods 5.2-5.3 (DSR and control), Results Figs. 2-6, Supplementary Figs. S4 and S12, Limitations, and Data Availability; official humml-lab/fmri-control repository.
appraisal_strengths: Individual models, held-out sequence reconstruction, free controlled trajectories, explicit zero-control/region perturbations, horizon sensitivity, and public code/preprocessed data.
appraisal_limitations: Small single-site cohort; the final test segment participates in model selection; abstract latent controls lack a physiological dose mapping, empirical intervention validation, formal calibration, external validation, and hazard testing.
source_status: Primary peer-reviewed full text and supplementary captions inspected; official code/data repository checked.

title: A data-driven Alzheimer's disease progression simulator for retrospective validation and prospective Phase III power design.
domain: Alzheimer disease progression and anti-amyloid Phase III trial simulation
dataset_or_cohort: ADNI amyloid-positive longitudinal cohort plus published aggregate results from six anti-amyloid randomized trials.
sample_scale: 351 ADNI participants with 1,256 visits; 100 simulations of 150 subjects per arm for centiloid analyses and 500 virtual trials per power design across 50-800 subjects per arm
institution_count: ADNI is multisite and six external trials are represented; exact institution count is NI
split_strategy: Natural-history dynamics are learned from ADNI; trial-specific amyloid-clearance calibration and leave-one-trial-out effect/variance calibration use published trial aggregates, so external comparisons are not fully frozen
observation_process: Irregular longitudinal amyloid PET, tau PET, MRI atrophy, and clinical measures; simulated trial visits every 3 months.
missingness: Missing biomarker observations are excluded from the likelihood rather than globally imputed
censoring_or_competing_events: Trial dropout, death, and competing events are NI and are not explicitly simulated
state: Latent disease state learned from amyloid, tau, MRI-derived atrophy, and clinical modalities, with trial-specific baseline latent initialization.
observation_decoder: Variational-autoencoder decoders map latent trajectories back to observed biomarkers and cognition
action: Anti-amyloid intervention represented as a piecewise modification of amyloid-clearance dynamics; placebo is the no-intervention comparator.
action_provenance: Simulated treatment profiles calibrated to published aggregate amyloid reductions from six RCTs.
transition_mechanism: Masked amyloid-cascade neural ODE in latent space with VAE observation models.
maximum_horizon: 18 months for four trial emulations and 27 months for gantenerumab, with results at multiple intermediate visits
rollout_regime: Free-running latent ODE trajectories for placebo and treated arms, repeated 500 times per trial design.
capability_claim: Counterfactual — compares simulated placebo and alternative anti-amyloid interventions and estimates treatment effects/power.
baselines: Linear mixed-effects, ridge regression, gradient boosting, observed placebo arms, and alternative calibration settings
state_fidelity_metrics: Multimodal reconstruction/trajectory comparisons and aggregate clinical endpoint agreement with published trials; exact metrics vary by modality and trial.
transition_metrics: Longitudinal trajectories and treatment-effect estimates at repeated visits through 18 or 27 months.
rollout_stability: Power curves and endpoint agreement are reported by trial duration/sample size; repeated simulations assess Monte Carlo stability
action_sensitivity: Six drug-specific clearance profiles and alternative treatment scenarios; treatment magnitude/timing are explicitly encoded, though calibrated from target-drug aggregate data.
calibration_and_uncertainty: Repeated virtual trials provide empirical variability and power; no reliability diagram, interval coverage, calibration slope, or equivalent formal predictive calibration
external_validation: Aggregate retrospective comparison with six RCTs; not fully frozen because baseline state and amyloid kinetics are trial-specific and calibrated to published trial information.
decision_utility: Prospective power and sample-size design for Phase III trials, compared with statistical and machine-learning simulators.
safety_evaluation: NI/negative: adverse events such as ARIA, treatment discontinuation, and treatment-related hazard are not modeled
statistical_analysis: Five-fold predictive-baseline cross-validation; 100 replicated 150-per-arm centiloid simulations; 500 virtual trials per power design with 50-800 subjects per arm
causal_language: Uses causal-intervention and counterfactual terminology for amyloid lowering and downstream outcomes
estimand: Treated-minus-placebo biomarker or CDR-SB endpoint difference and the resulting empirical power at specified trial horizons
confounding_strategy: No individual-level treatment-confounding adjustment; ADNI supplies natural-history dynamics and trial aggregate changes calibrate intervention effects
positivity_and_overlap: No propensity, overlap, or support diagnostic for treatment response is reported
counterfactual_validation: Retrospective reproduction of published trial-level trajectories/endpoints provides partial validation, not individual counterfactual truth
code_access: Partial/public — training code is inspectable at the paper-reported Inria GitLab; trial-simulation code is stated as planned upon acceptance.
weights_access: NI: pretrained model weights or a fixed model checkpoint are not clearly reported as public
data_access: Credentialed — ADNI data require application; published RCT aggregates are publicly reported.
preprocessing_reproducibility: Partial — cohort criteria, modalities, equations, and pseudocode are detailed, but the full trial pipeline and fitted parameters are not yet released.
randomness: Monte Carlo repetitions are explicit; complete random-seed values and deterministic environment details are NI
evidence_anchors: medRxiv v1 full text, DOI 10.64898/2026.05.03.26352317: Results, Tables 1-2 and Figs. 1-5; Methods sections on ADNI cohort, latent ODE dynamics, intervention calibration, virtual trials, and power.
appraisal_strengths: Multiple trial targets, multimodal latent dynamics, horizon-specific outcomes, repeated power simulations, and inspectable public code
appraisal_limitations: Preprint; trial-specific adaptation, no full causal identification or support analysis, no safety modeling, and incomplete release of trial code/weights.
source_status: Full medRxiv v1 preprint PDF inspected

title: A digital twin for hospital antimicrobial resistance forecasting and constrained intervention optimisation
domain: Hospital epidemiology; antimicrobial resistance; synthetic contact-network digital twin
dataset_or_cohort: Author-developed synthetic hospital simulator under canonical, partial-observation, shock, superspreader, surveillance, and distribution-shift regimes
sample_scale: 10 wards, 200 patients, 300 staff; 60-day canonical and 360-day shifted trajectories; 12 independent replicates per family
institution_count: NA: fully synthetic hospital rather than an observed institutional cohort
split_strategy: Trajectory-level train/validation/test partitions with disjoint simulator seed ranges; matched counterfactual branches share initial state and exogenous random stream
observation_process: Daily directed weighted patient-staff contact graphs; patient/staff attributes, admissions, antibiotic exposure, infection/resistance, isolation, screening and surveillance
missingness: Partial-observation experiments explicitly delay, reduce, or compress surveillance; no real-world missing-data mechanism
censoring_or_competing_events: Admissions, discharges and importation are generated by the simulator; no observational censoring problem
state: Daily hospital graph with node features, ward/contact structure, colonization/infection/resistance status, antibiotic exposure and containment state
observation_decoder: Forecast of endogenous spread versus importation and intervention-conditioned future resistant burden/action ranking
action: Library of hospital-wide screening and isolation policies subject to budgets, maximum-use and cooldown constraints
action_provenance: Explicit simulated screening/isolation policies applied to cloned hospital states
transition_mechanism: Mechanistic agent/contact simulator plus GraphSAGE and temporal transformer forecasting; MILP selects a constrained policy
maximum_horizon: 7 observed days to forecast or branch 7 future days
rollout_regime: Learned fixed-H=7 forecasts from branched simulator states; matched policy evaluation uses a common past and common exogenous random stream, while the mechanistic hospital simulator—not the learned forecaster—runs freely.
capability_claim: Planning: forecast action-conditioned outcomes and optimize constrained screening/isolation policy
baselines: Predictive baselines and feature/contact ablations; baseline containment protocol serves as no-change comparator
state_fidelity_metrics: AUROC, accuracy, F1, sensitivity and specificity for spread-source classification
transition_metrics: Within-state action-ranking accuracy, top-2 accuracy, strict improvement, non-worsening rate, regret and AUROC
rollout_stability: Distribution-shift and surveillance stress tests; non-worsening and regret reported; no formal long-horizon learned-model drift curve
action_sensitivity: Ground-truth versus partial observation, contact-weight and node-feature ablations, delayed/frequent surveillance changes, and multiple policy actions
calibration_and_uncertainty: Threshold fragility under shift is discussed; no reliability diagram, ECE, slope/intercept, or interval-coverage calibration
external_validation: Only synthetic regime shifts and retraining/zero-shot transfer; no external hospital or simulated-to-real validation
decision_utility: Seventy held-out states support action ranking; MILP demonstrates constrained policy selection in simulation
safety_evaluation: Containment burden and non-worsening are measured; budget/max-use/cooldown constraints and stress regimes are tested; no clinical deployment safety
statistical_analysis: Independent replicates, held-out seed ranges and reported performance distributions; exact inferential test details are limited
causal_language: The paper labels a causal/intervention branch and generates matched counterfactual futures from identical states
estimand: Baseline-relative 7-day resistant-infection burden and policy value within the specified simulator
confounding_strategy: Simulator structure and matched exogenous random streams remove simulated confounding; no real-world confounding analysis
positivity_and_overlap: Within-simulator actions are available by construction; real-hospital positivity/overlap is NA
counterfactual_validation: Matched simulator branches provide synthetic counterfactual ground truth only
code_access: Public implementations: https://github.com/harrytr/dt_amr_predictive and https://github.com/harrytr/dt_amr_causal
weights_access: Unclear: pretrained learned-model weights were not stated as released
data_access: Publicly regenerable synthetic trajectories and driver scripts; no real patient data
preprocessing_reproducibility: Simulator, feature construction, seed partitions and model/optimization workflow are described and coded
randomness: Disjoint seed ranges and 12 independent replicates are reported
evidence_anchors: medRxiv version 1 full text: Methods on the synthetic hospital, T=7/H=7 temporal graph task, partial observation, common-state/common-noise intervention branching, and constrained MILP; Results on surveillance and distribution shifts and within-state policy ranking; Code Availability links the predictive and causal repositories.
appraisal_strengths: Matched branches, explicit action library, action baselines, stress tests and constrained optimization
appraisal_limitations: Preprint-only and entirely synthetic evidence; the learned forecaster is fixed-horizon rather than recursively free-running; no real-hospital validation, formal calibration, or clinical deployment hazard evaluation.
source_status: full_text_inspected

title: DRIFT: Direct-Recursive Intervention-Conditioned Forecasting of ICU Physiological Trajectories
domain: ICU physiological time-series forecasting with observed vasopressor conditioning
dataset_or_cohort: MIMIC-IV v3.1 development cohort and independently processed eICU-CRD v2.0 replication cohort
sample_scale: MIMIC-IV: 40,301 stays (28,210 train, 6,045 validation, 6,046 test); eICU: 55,093 stays (38,633 train, 8,115 validation, 8,345 test)
institution_count: MIMIC-IV is single-center; eICU test data span 131 hospitals and 212 hospital-ward pairs, all represented in training
split_strategy: Patient-disjoint MIMIC splits; patient-level 70/15/15 eICU hash split; independent preprocessing and training by database; eICU is cross-database but not hospital-held-out
observation_process: Twenty-seven physiological variables in one-hour bins with observation masks, elapsed times, time features, static context, and a future candidate vasopressor path
missingness: Past-only within-stay forward filling; remaining leading gaps use training-set medians; masks and elapsed times are retained; eICU mappings and normalization are fit on eICU training data only
censoring_or_competing_events: Adults with ICU length of stay at least 24 hours; first eligible stay retained; pre-index vasopressor exposure and death by hour 6 excluded; trajectories limited to first 72 ICU hours; no censoring or competing-risk model
state: Normalized 27-variable physiology plus masks, elapsed times, history encoding, direct latent states, recursively advanced latent states, time features, and static predictive context
observation_decoder: A shared decoder outputs all 27 future variables, followed by a local correction for HR, SBP, DBP, and MAP
action: Hourly binary exposure to any of dopamine, epinephrine, norepinephrine, phenylephrine, or vasopressin, encoded with exposure, onset, duration, and time since exposure
action_provenance: Recorded administered/input-event vasopressor exposure in MIMIC; positive infusion snapshots with a 120-minute carry in eICU; supplied paths are observed or donor-substituted predictive scenarios
transition_mechanism: Hybrid direct-recursive model: a TFT-style direct anchor predicts all future states, while a shared one-hour recursive latent transition supplies bounded low-dimensional corrections through a shared decoder
maximum_horizon: Up to 48 hours, with results at 8, 24, and 48 hours and integrated lead-wise evaluation over hours 1-48
rollout_regime: One call returns the full trajectory; the direct path is multi-output and causal in the action prefix, while an internal recursive state consumes its own preceding latent state hourly; the recursive path is never decoded independently
capability_claim: Action-conditioned factual forecasting; the paper explicitly rejects causal treatment-effect, counterfactual, policy, action-generation, and recommendation interpretations
baselines: Persistence, GRU with/without action, mask-decay GRU, Transformer with/without action, TFT with/without dynamic action, capacity-matched TFT-Large, forecast-loss-transfer TFT-Large-FL, PatchTST-action, iTransformer-action, PPO-inspired DirRecMO-8, and seven component ablations
state_fidelity_metrics: Normalized endpoint and integrated 27-variable MSE; raw and observed-only MAP MAE; HR/SBP/DBP/MAP MAE; subgroup directional counts
transition_metrics: Endpoint MSE and MAP MAE at 8/24/48 hours; integrated 1-48-hour trajectory errors; recursive-direct latent discrepancy, final-direct MSE, and correction RMS by lead
rollout_stability: Horizon-specific and integrated trajectory errors; latent discrepancy and correction magnitude at leads 1, 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, and 48; changed-path prediction response aligned to first divergence
action_sensitivity: Action/no-action baselines; full-stream and future-only donor-path replacement; changed-window analyses; first-divergence timing; removal of recursive response/timing; residual-budget sensitivity
calibration_and_uncertainty: No predictive uncertainty, formal calibration, interval coverage, or abstention; confidence intervals quantify comparative sampling uncertainty only
external_validation: Independent eICU database replication with source-specific retraining and preprocessing; all test hospitals and wards occur in training, and the model is adapted rather than frozen
decision_utility: No clinician, treatment-policy, recommendation, or prospective workflow evaluation; utility is forecasting accuracy and input-dependence auditing
safety_evaluation: No clinical hazard/severity framework or intervention-safety test; exploratory subgroup reversals are descriptive and not a safety evaluation
statistical_analysis: Three seeds (42-44); 2,000 or 5,000 hierarchical bootstrap samples over seeds and stays; plus-one two-sided probabilities; Benjamini-Hochberg correction; shared checkpoint-selection robustness; confidence intervals reported
causal_language: Explicitly states that actions are predictive covariates, DRIFT estimates neither a policy nor counterfactual outcomes, replacement audits input dependence, and results do not establish causal effects or clinical benefit
estimand: Recorded-path factual trajectory prediction and shifted-input error-gap comparisons with the observed outcome held fixed; no intervention-effect or regime-value estimand
confounding_strategy: Two treatment-likelihood features are fitted on training data as predictive context only and are not causal weights; no causal confounding adjustment
positivity_and_overlap: No causal positivity analysis; donor mappings use exact mask strata and the paper audits sparse all-zero replacements, but this assesses perturbation prevalence rather than treatment-effect overlap
counterfactual_validation: None; donor substitution keeps the observed outcome unchanged and is explicitly not validation of an alternative-treatment trajectory
code_access: A public release is promised upon publication; study-specific code is unavailable at the coding cutoff
weights_access: Unavailable; sensitive checkpoints are stated to be excluded from the planned public package
data_access: Credentialed research access to MIMIC-IV and eICU-CRD; restricted patient-level tensors, predictions, rosters, and checkpoints are not redistributed
preprocessing_reproducibility: Highly detailed cohort flow, variables, imputation, action alignment, architectures, losses, training stages, checkpoint rules, hardware, evaluation rosters, bootstrap, and cross-database mappings
randomness: Seeds 42, 43, and 44; stochastic donor mappings and hierarchical bootstrap procedures are specified; deterministic algorithms are not enforced
evidence_anchors: Main text pp. 1-7 for claim boundary, model, datasets, replacement audit, results, and limitations; Tables 1-4 pp. 6-7; Appendices B-C pp. 10-20 for cohort, preprocessing, losses, seeds, and checkpoint robustness; Appendix D pp. 21-24 for action audits; Appendices F-H pp. 25-34 for rollout diagnostics, code status, and eICU replication
appraisal_strengths: Strong causal boundary language; detailed action provenance and timing; action-agnostic and perturbation audits; multi-horizon and lead-wise diagnostics; patient-disjoint cross-database replication; extensive statistical robustness
appraisal_limitations: Absolute gains are small and concentrated on MAP; eICU requires retraining and is not site-held-out; binary exposure omits dose and co-interventions; no predictive calibration, clinical decision utility, or causal effect validation; code is not yet public
source_status: Primary arXiv v1 full text inspected on 2026-09-12; open access
